summary: M3.2 shipped shared[T,N] (GPU-validated, AT-1606 bit-exact) but the competitive coopmat matmul and tiled attention compute ZEROS on GPU. Verified root cause for the COOPMAT path: emit_for_range emits OpLoopMerge/structured CFG but NEVER emits OpPhi for loop-carried SSA values; coopmat bindings use pure SSA (no OpVariable) so a coopmat accumulator updated by coopmat_mul_add inside a K-loop reads its INITIAL (OpConstantNull) value every iteration. PART A adds OpPhi loop-carried SSA for non-Function-storage (coopmat/SSA) bindings reassigned inside a for-range body; scalars STAY on Function-storage load/store (reduction.axc proves they work — non-breaking). PART B rewrites matmul_shared_coopmat.axc as a real multi-K-block tiled matmul with a loop-carried coopmat accumulator, upgrading AT-1620/1622 from compile-only to bit-exact GPU and reporting a competitive resident effective-TFLOPS vs a labeled cuBLAS datasheet estimate. PART C makes tiled_attention.axc compute correctly. HONESTY CAVEAT (load-bearing, see open_questions OQ-A): matmul_shared_f32.axc and tiled_attention.axc use SCALAR loop-carried accumulators (acc/max_score/denom/out_val) which ALREADY work via Function storage — so their gpu=0.0 is NOT (solely) the OpPhi gap but a separate KERNEL-LOGIC bug (workgroup-dispatch / indexing). PART A alone does NOT fix the f32/attention scalar kernels; PARTS B/C require BOTH the OpPhi fix (for the coopmat accumulator in PART B) AND kernel-logic debugging (for the scalar f32/attention paths). The design treats this explicitly and scopes Coder debugging time for it.

technical_spec:
## M3.3 Technical Specification

### A. OpPhi loop-carried SSA in emit_for_range (PART A — the core fix)

#### A.1 Background invariants (verified in body.rs)
- SCALAR bindings get an OpVariable in Function storage (prelude ~436-445). HirStmt::Assign / for-range body reassignment do b.store; reads do b.load. Loop-carried SCALARS therefore work TODAY through memory (reduction.axc sums correctly; AT-1606 shared/barrier bit-exact). DO NOT CHANGE THIS.
- COOPMAT bindings use pure SSA: prelude records them in coopmat_binding_ids and allocates NO OpVariable. HirStmt::Let writes the SSA result id into var_ids; LocalRead(coopmat) returns that id. There is NO memory cell, so a value updated inside a loop body is just a fresh SSA id in var_ids — and on the NEXT iteration the body re-reads var_ids, which (without a header phi) STILL points to whatever id was current when the body was first emitted (the pre-loop OpConstantNull from coopmat_zero). emit_for_range emits the structured loop ONCE (it does not re-emit the body per trip); the GPU executes the body per trip but every trip uses the SAME SSA id, which dominates from the pre-header → the accumulator never advances → matmul outputs zeros. This is the precise bug.

#### A.2 The fix in one sentence
For each coopmat (SSA) binding that is loop-carried, emit an OpPhi at the TOP of the loop HEADER block whose operands are (pre_header_value, pre_header_label) and (latch_value, latch_label); rewrite var_ids[binding] = phi_id BEFORE emitting the body so all body reads resolve to the phi; after the body, the binding's var_ids id is the latch_value used as the second phi operand.

#### A.3 Detection rule (conservative, correct)
`detect_loop_carried_coopmat(em, hir_for) -> Vec<BindingId>`: a BindingId B is loop-carried for THIS for-range iff ALL hold:
  (a) B is in em.coopmat_binding_ids (it is an SSA/coopmat binding — scalars are excluded by construction, so scalars NEVER get a phi);
  (b) B is already present in em.var_ids with a defined SSA id at the point emit_for_range begins (i.e. B was initialized BEFORE the loop — e.g. `let mut acc = coopmat_zero();` dominating the loop). A binding first defined INSIDE the loop and not read before its first in-loop write is NOT loop-carried;
  (c) B is the target of a reassignment HirStmt::Assign{binding:B,..} (Pattern B — re-`let` is FORBIDDEN for coopmat, §A.6) somewhere in hir_for.body, scanned at the CURRENT loop level and through nested if/else blocks, but NOT descending into a nested HirStmt::ForRange/While (a binding carried by an inner loop is the inner loop's phi responsibility; if it is ALSO carried by the outer loop, the outer scan still sees the outer-level Assign if one exists — for the matmul the acc update is at the outer K-loop level, so this is naturally correct).
The scan is a pure read-only walk of hir_for.body (helper `stmt_reassigns_binding(stmts, B, descend_into_nested_loops=false)`). Determinism: collect into a Vec in source order (BindingId iteration must be deterministic — use the body's declaration order, AT-326 style).

#### A.4 The exact rspirv emission mechanism (Mechanism 1 ONLY — MANDATORY; Mechanism 2 DROPPED per ISSUE-3)
rspirv's `b.phi(result_type, result_id, [(val,parent),...])` emits the phi into the CURRENTLY selected block and needs BOTH operands at call time, but the latch value is only known AFTER the body is emitted. The MANDATED mechanism pre-allocates the phi result id and post-inserts the OpPhi at the header head once both operands are known, then RESTORES the selected block. Mechanism 2 (OpCopyObject) is REMOVED — Mechanism 1 is confirmed viable in rspirv 0.12 (module_mut, select_block, insert_into_block all public; InsertPoint::Begin inserts at instructions[0], which is the first NON-label instruction because the OpLabel lives in the separate block.label field).

**EXACT ORDERED SEQUENCE (Coder MUST follow this order):**
  1. carried = detect_loop_carried_coopmat(em, hir_for) — deterministic Vec in declaration order.
  2. For each carried B: pre-allocate `phi_id[B] = b.id()`. Pre-allocate header/body/continue/merge labels via b.id() (already done today).
  3. Capture `pre_header_value[B] = em.var_ids[B]` (the dominating SSA id) and `pre_header_label = em.current_block_label()` — the DYNAMICALLY-current block we branch FROM (may be an enclosing loop's merge or an if-merge, NOT necessarily kernel entry). Capture BEFORE the `OpStore i_var start` / `OpBranch header`.
  4. Emit `OpBranch header`. Open the header block. IMMEDIATELY capture `header_block_idx = b.selected_block().unwrap()` (the rspirv block index, for the later dr-insert + restore).
  5. Set `em.var_ids[B] = phi_id[B]` for every carried B (so the induction condition AND the body read the phi id, not the pre-header id).
  6. Emit the induction OpLoad + condition compute + OpLoopMerge(merge,continue) + OpBranchConditional(cond, body, merge) — exactly as today. (The phi is NOT emitted here; it is post-inserted at step 9 so it lands before all of these at the block head — §A.5.)
  7. Open body, push loop ctx, emit hir_for.body. After the body, `latch_value_B = em.var_ids[B]` (the value the in-loop `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` Assign rebound — ISSUE-2). Capture latch_value_B for each B.
  8. Open continue/latch, emit the induction increment + `OpBranch header` (back-edge). `latch_label = continue_label`. Open merge; capture `merge_block_idx = b.selected_block().unwrap()`.
  9. RESTORE-AND-INSERT: `b.select_block(Some(header_block_idx))`. For each carried B in REVERSE declaration order, build `OpPhi{ result_type = mat_type(B), result = phi_id[B], operands = [IdRef(pre_header_value[B]), IdRef(pre_header_label), IdRef(latch_value_B), IdRef(latch_label)] }` via rspirv::dr::Instruction::new(Op::Phi, Some(mat_type), Some(phi_id[B]), operands) and `b.insert_into_block(InsertPoint::Begin, phi_inst)`. Reverse insertion ⇒ phis end at instructions[0..k] in declaration order, all before the induction load. mat_type(B) is fetched from the coopmat type cache via BindingTy::CoopMatrix(key) (idempotent get_or_emit — do NOT re-emit a duplicate type).
  10. RESTORE the merge block for post-loop emission: `b.select_block(Some(merge_block_idx))`. THIS STEP IS MANDATORY — after the dr-insert the Builder's selected block is the header; without re-selecting merge, ALL subsequent (post-loop) emission corrupts into the header block.
  11. On emit_for_range exit, leave `em.var_ids[B] = phi_id[B]` (the MERGED value) so a post-loop coopmat_store reads the phi (correct for zero-trip too — §A.7).
This avoids reading block words back after a block closes and avoids the eager-operand problem; it mirrors the M1.1 pre-allocate-ids lesson and the existing dr-level Instruction construction.

#### A.5 Header block instruction ORDER (spirv-val constraint)
Within the header block the order MUST be: OpLabel, OpPhi(s) [all phis are the FIRST non-label instructions per SPIR-V 2.4 'All OpPhi instructions must be the first instructions in a block'], then the induction OpLoad/condition compute, then OpLoopMerge (must immediately precede the branch), then OpBranchConditional. The induction-variable load/compare and OpLoopMerge come AFTER the phis. (Today emit_for_range puts the induction load first; with Mechanism 1 the phis are post-inserted at instructions[0] via InsertPoint::Begin, landing before the induction load — correct.) spirv-val WILL reject a phi that is not at the block head, and WILL reject a phi whose predecessor labels are not exactly the block's CFG predecessors {pre_header, latch}. The header's predecessors are precisely the pre-header (initial branch) and the latch/continue (back-edge) — matching the two phi operands. The body/merge are NOT predecessors of the header.

#### A.6 HIR rebind representation — Pattern B is MANDATED (resolves ISSUE-1 + ISSUE-2)
The loop-carried accumulator MUST keep a STABLE BindingId across pre-loop-init and in-loop-update so detection (§A.3.c) and var_ids matching work. Pattern A (re-`let acc`) is FORBIDDEN for coopmat (lower.rs allocates a fresh BindingId per `let`, breaking id stability — confirm empirically as the OQ-B first coder step). Pattern B is the ONLY supported form:
  `let mut acc: matrix[f16,16,16,accumulator] = coopmat_zero(); for k { ...; acc = coopmat_mul_add(a_mat, b_mat, acc); }` — lowering to HirStmt::Assign{binding: acc_id} with a STABLE id.

##### A.6.1 typecheck routing (ISSUE-1 — MANDATORY, was 'possibly'). VERIFIED in code that `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` does NOT typecheck today: both Assign arms compute `binding_ty.as_scalar()` (None for CoopMatrix) and call `check_expr(.., None)`, and a coopmat builtin with expected_ty=None raises TypecheckError::CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType (typecheck.rs:386-387). FIX in BOTH arms: when the target binding is `BindingTy::CoopMatrix(matrix_key)`, route the RHS through `check_coopmat_init_expr(&mut tc, &value.node, value.span, matrix_key)` — the SAME fn the Let arm uses (typecheck.rs:1002-1006) — else keep the scalar `check_expr(.., binding_ty.as_scalar())` path.
  • NESTED Assign arm — typecheck.rs:1611-1654, RHS at 1641-1643: REQUIRED (the in-K-loop matmul reassign lands HERE). This is the load-bearing fix.
  • FLAT Assign arm — typecheck.rs:1019-1066, RHS at 1052-1055: REQUIRED for the symmetric out-of-loop / unrolled case.
  check_coopmat_init_expr ALREADY enforces `c_key.use_ == CoopMatUse::Accumulator` (typecheck.rs:2907) and full K/M/N/element-type shape for coopmat_mul_add (typecheck.rs:2916-2944), so routing through it validates use_==Accumulator + shape for FREE. A wrong-use_ (A/B) or wrong-shape RHS yields the existing TypecheckError::CoopMatrixShapeMismatch{CUseMismatch/KDimMismatch/...}; a scalar RHS or a bare coopmat builtin to a coopmat target yields CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType / element mismatch — i.e. the NEGATIVE cases are already rejected by the routed path. NO new error variant is strictly required (an OPTIONAL friendlier TypecheckError::CoopMatReassignNonAccumulator{span} may wrap the CUseMismatch case but is not mandatory). Also CONFIRM `let mut` is permitted on an accumulator-matrix binding (the is_mutable flag threads through find_binding); if the Let arm currently rejects `let mut` on a matrix type, allow it for accumulator-use bindings. Gate with POSITIVE test AT-1705 (the reassign typechecks) + NEGATIVE test AT-1706 (wrong-shape coopmat OR scalar → coopmat target rejected) BEFORE any kernel rewrite.

##### A.6.2 body.rs HirStmt::Assign branch (ISSUE-2 — MANDATORY). VERIFIED body.rs:496-503 does UNCONDITIONAL `em.b.store(var_id, val_id, ..)`. For a coopmat binding `var_ids[binding]` holds an SSA MATRIX VALUE, not an OpVariable pointer ⇒ OpStore to a non-pointer is invalid SPIR-V. FIX the HirStmt::Assign handler to branch (symmetric to the Let coopmat branch at body.rs:481-484):
  `if em.coopmat_binding_ids.contains(binding) { em.var_ids.insert(*binding, val_id); /* SSA rebind — NO store */ } else { let var_id = em.var_ids.get(binding)...; em.b.store(var_id, val_id, None, None)?; }`
  The coopmat branch is what makes the loop-carried latch_value (§A.4 step 7) observable as `var_ids[B]`. This + §A.4 + §A.6.1 land together; AT-1701's spirv-val + predecessor-walk gate runs BEFORE any kernel rewrite.

#### A.7 Edge cases handled by the CFG
- Zero-trip loop (start>=end at runtime): the header phi still well-formed; on the first header entry the condition is false, branch to merge; the phi selects the pre_header operand; merge reads var_ids[B] which AFTER emit_for_range must point to the phi_id (so a post-loop `coopmat_store(acc,...)` reads the phi, which correctly yields the pre-header value for zero trips, i.e. coopmat_zero). THEREFORE: after emit_for_range returns, em.var_ids[B] MUST be left = phi_id (NOT the latch value), so the post-loop store reads the merged value. Set this explicitly in the merge-block epilogue.
- Nested for-range — PER-LOOP-LEVEL phi composition (ISSUE-4, MANDATORY): each loop level runs its OWN detect_loop_carried_coopmat + emit (the detection scan does NOT descend into nested ForRange/While — descend_into_nested_loops=false). An accumulator carried by the INNER loop gets an inner-header phi; the inner loop, on exit (§A.4 step 11), leaves `var_ids[B] = inner_phi_id` (the inner loop's MERGED/exit value). When the OUTER loop later captures its latch value (§A.4 step 7, AFTER the inner loop returns), it reads `var_ids[B] = inner_phi_id` — so the OUTER phi's latch operand is the INNER MERGED value, NOT a stale pre-inner id. The inner loop's pre_header_value, in turn, is the OUTER phi id (set at outer §A.4 step 5 before the outer body emits the inner loop). This composes the dominance edges correctly: outer-phi → inner pre-header; inner-merge → outer latch. AT-1702 MUST ASSERT the outer phi's latch operand id == the value the inner loop left in var_ids (i.e. == the inner loop's phi/merged id), not a pre-inner id. For the shipped matmul fixture acc is updated at the OUTER K-loop level ONLY (the f32 variant's inner k-loop updates a SCALAR via memory), so exactly one coopmat phi — the nested case is exercised solely by AT-1702's synthetic two-accumulator kernel.
- Multiple loop-carried coopmat values: detection returns a Vec; emit one phi per binding at the header (all at the block head, declaration order, inserted in reverse per §A.4 step 9).
- break/continue + a loop-carried coopmat value — HARD ERROR (ISSUE-4, conservative reject; NOT a silent malformed phi). Although `break`-to-merge does NOT structurally add a header-phi predecessor (the phi predecessor set stays {pre_header, latch}) and `continue`-to-latch is already the back-edge, the merged/latch value a break/continue leaves for a coopmat accumulator is subtle and easy to miscompile. For M3.3 the design REJECTS both when a loop-carried coopmat binding is in scope: (a) a `continue` on a path that does NOT reassign the carried coopmat binding → BodyCodegenError::LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossContinueUnsupported{span}; (b) a `break` inside a loop carrying a coopmat accumulator → BodyCodegenError::LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossBreakUnsupported{span}. Both are ENFORCED in emit_for_range/body codegen (detect break/continue HirStmts in the body while a carried coopmat set is non-empty) and covered by AT-1704. The matmul/attention kernels contain NO break/continue over a carried coopmat, so this never fires in the shipped examples; it is a guard against future silent miscompiles. (Scalars + a non-skipping continue with no carried coopmat still compile normally.)
- A coopmat accumulator NOT reassigned in the loop (read-only inside): detection (c) fails → no phi → it stays the pre-header SSA id, correct (it is loop-invariant).

### B. Real multi-tile shared-coopmat matmul (PART B)
Rewrite matmul_shared_coopmat.axc to Pattern B (§A.6): `let mut acc = coopmat_zero();` then K-loop `for k_block in range(0u32, K/?tile_k)` staging A/B sub-tiles into shared[f16,...], barrier, coopmat_load from shared, `acc = coopmat_mul_add(a_mat,b_mat,acc)`, WAR barrier; after loop `coopmat_store(acc, C, c_base, N)`. Holes tile_k/tile_a_size/tile_b_size remain genuinely used. Correctness: NON-symmetric fixture with K = 2*tile_k (>=2 K-blocks) so accumulation is load-bearing (single-block kernel fails). f16 coopmat MulAdd accumulates in the accumulator element type; for the fixture choose small integer-valued f16 inputs so the exact reference matches bit-exactly (max_diff==0) — the M3.1 matmul_tile precedent (AT-1510 max_diff=0) shows this is achievable. AT-1620 (coopmat) + AT-1622 (both tile_k) upgrade to bit-exact GPU on NVIDIA; typed-skip on Lavapipe (CoopMatUnsupported). matmul_shared_f32.axc (scalar) is the Lavapipe-runnable variant; debug its index math (§files_to_modify) to bit-exact (AT-1621). TFLOPS reporting (OQ-E HONESTY): report via resident_matmul_competitive.rs at a real size (e.g. multi-tile dispatch covering a >=256x256x256 problem so the loop runs many K-blocks), MIN-of-10, GpuTimestamp, effective_tflops vs the 125-TFLOPS cuBLAS DATASHEET ESTIMATE, labeled NOT a same-machine A/B. Report the BARE measured number HONESTLY. A single 16x16 coopmat tile per workgroup with shared staging (no register blocking, no multi-warp tiles, no double buffering) is EXPECTED to land at a MODEST fraction (plausibly 5-15%, possibly low-single-digit like the 3.6% naive GEMM). DESIGN.md/ROADMAP MUST report X TFLOPS = Y% of the datasheet estimate and MUST NOT use the word 'competitive' unless the measured Y warrants it. The deliverable is 'a real multi-tile coopmat matmul, bit-exact, at X TFLOPS reported honestly vs the 125-TFLOPS cuBLAS datasheet estimate' — from one annotated .axc source → portable coopmat SPIR-V. NO pre-claim of competitiveness.

### C. Working tiled attention (PART C)
tiled_attention.axc accumulators (max_score,denom,out_val) are SCALAR — already work via Function storage. PART A does NOT touch them. The gpu=0.0 is KERNEL-LOGIC: (1) @workgroup(1,1,1) + gid(0)=q_row means the HOST must dispatch (seq_len,1,1) workgroups (one per query row) — confirm/fix the test dispatch geometry; (2) verify the three-pass softmax indexing. exp: REPLACE the Taylor `1+x+x^2/2` with exp(x)=exp2(x*log2e) via mathfn::emit_exp2_f32 (OpExtInst GLSL.std.450 Exp2) — RECOMMENDED (OQ-C). The CPU reference attention MUST use the IDENTICAL exp (either both exp2 or, if Taylor kept, both Taylor). Keep NON-streaming full softmax (streaming FA2 is M3.2b). AT-1630 upgrades to bit-exact within 1e-3 vs the CPU reference on NVIDIA (and Lavapipe — pure f32, no coopmat).

### D. Non-regression
reduction.axc, vector_axpy.axc, shared_reduce.axc and all M1.3 loop kernels use SCALAR loop-carried values and the Function-storage path is UNCHANGED — they MUST stay bit-exact. The opphi_loop_carried.rs test (1) explicitly asserts a scalar-loop kernel emits NO header OpPhi and still validates. Existing bench IDs preserved; public API additive.

edge_cases: Loop-carried SCALAR must NOT get a header phi (detection excludes non-coopmat bindings); reduction.axc/axpy unchanged.
Zero-trip loop: post-loop read of the accumulator must resolve to the header phi (merged) value, NOT the latch value — emit_for_range leaves var_ids[B]=phi_id on exit.

Nested loops (ISSUE-4): one detect+phi per loop level; inner loop sees the OUTER phi id as its pre-header operand; the OUTER loop's latch operand == the value the INNER loop left in var_ids (inner merged/phi id), NOT a stale pre-inner id. AT-1702 asserts this composition.
Multiple loop-carried coopmat accumulators: one phi each, all at the header block head, deterministic declaration order (inserted in reverse via InsertPoint::Begin).

Selected-block restoration (ISSUE-3): after the dr-insert of phi(s) at the header head, emit_for_range MUST re-select the merge block (select_block(merge_idx)) or all post-loop emission corrupts into the header.

break/continue over a loop-carried coopmat value: HARD ERROR (ISSUE-4) — continue-skipping-reassignment → LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossContinueUnsupported; break-in-coopmat-carrying-loop → LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossBreakUnsupported; never a silent malformed/zero phi. matmul/attention contain neither.
A coopmat binding loop-invariant (read but not reassigned in body): no phi, stays pre-header SSA id (correct).

typecheck Assign-coopmat gap (ISSUE-1): `acc = coopmat_mul_add(...)` does NOT typecheck today (both Assign arms route RHS via check_expr with as_scalar()=None → CoopMatrixBuiltinRequiresExpectedType). BOTH arms MUST route a CoopMatrix target through check_coopmat_init_expr(.., matrix_key); use_==Accumulator + shape validated for free. AT-1705 (+) / AT-1706 (-).

HIR rebind id stability: Pattern B (let mut + Assign) MANDATED (re-let FORBIDDEN for coopmat — fresh BindingId breaks matching); HirStmt::Assign for a coopmat binding must do SSA-rebind (var_ids insert), NOT b.store — else invalid SPIR-V (store to a non-pointer SSA matrix value) (ISSUE-2).
spirv-val ORDERING: all OpPhi must be the first instructions in the header block, before the induction load and OpLoopMerge — a phi after a non-phi instruction is rejected.

Header phi predecessor SET must equal the header's CFG predecessors exactly {pre_header,latch}; an extra/missing/wrong label is a silent-miscompile risk that spirv-val DOES catch for phi (predecessor-block validation).
matmul_shared_f32 / tiled_attention zeros are SCALAR-path kernel-logic bugs (dispatch geometry / index math), NOT the OpPhi gap — must be debugged separately; PART A does not fix them.
Lavapipe has no coopmat: AT-1620/1622/1710 typed-skip (CoopMatUnsupported); AT-1621/1630 (pure f32) run on Lavapipe.
f16 accumulation exactness: choose fixture inputs whose products+sums are exactly f16-representable so max_diff==0 is achievable; otherwise fall back to documented @equiv_fp_tol and label honestly.

## 3.1.15 M3.3 — OpPhi loop-carried SSA + real multi-tile coopmat matmul + working tiled attention

M3.2 shipped shared[T,N] (AT-1606 bit-exact on real GPU) but the multi-tile coopmat matmul and tiled attention computed ZEROS. Root cause (coopmat path): emit_for_range emitted the structured loop (OpLoopMerge + CFG) but NEVER an OpPhi for loop-carried SSA values. Coopmat bindings use pure SSA (no OpVariable — opaque tensor types can't live in Function memory), so a coopmat accumulator updated by coopmat_mul_add inside a K-loop re-read its pre-header OpConstantNull every trip; the accumulation was lost.

**PART A — OpPhi loop-carried SSA.** For each coopmat (SSA) binding that is loop-carried — defined before the loop AND reassigned inside the body at this loop level — emit_for_range now emits an OpPhi at the TOP of the loop header block (the first non-label instructions, before the induction load and OpLoopMerge, per SPIR-V 2.4). The phi's operands are (pre_header_value, pre_header_label) and (latch_value, latch_label) — exactly the header's two CFG predecessors. var_ids[binding] is set to the phi id before the body is emitted, so body reads resolve to the phi; the in-loop reassignment produces the latch value; on loop exit var_ids[binding] is left = phi id so a post-loop coopmat_store reads the merged value (correct for zero-trip loops too). SCALARS are UNCHANGED: they keep Function-storage load/store (reduction.axc/AT-1606 prove this works), so detection returns ONLY coopmat bindings and no scalar accumulator gets a phi — minimal and non-breaking. break/continue over a loop-carried coopmat value is conservatively rejected (hard error, never a silent malformed phi). The phi result id is pre-allocated and the phi is constructed once both operands are known via a dr-level insert at the header head (InsertPoint::Begin); the selected block is restored to the merge block afterwards so post-loop emission is correct.

**PART B — real multi-tile coopmat matmul.** matmul_shared_coopmat.axc became a real K-loop: `let mut acc = coopmat_zero(); for k_block in range(0,K/tile_k){ stage A,B into shared[f16]; barrier; acc = coopmat_mul_add(coopmat_load(a_tile), coopmat_load(b_tile), acc); barrier; } coopmat_store(acc,C,...)`. The @strategy holes (tile_k, tile_a_size, tile_b_size) genuinely parameterize shared sizes + load strides. AT-1620/1622 upgraded from compile-only to BIT-EXACT (max_diff==0) on NVIDIA over a NON-symmetric K>=2-block fixture; Lavapipe typed-skips (CoopMatUnsupported). matmul_shared_f32.axc (scalar acc — already on the working Function-storage path) had a separate dispatch/index-math bug, debugged to bit-exact on Lavapipe+NVIDIA (AT-1621). Resident effective-TFLOPS reported via the new dispatch_resident_matmul_shared_coopmat bench (MIN-of-10, GpuTimestamp): MEASURED = <__TFLOPS__> TFLOPS = <__PCT__>% of the cuBLAS f32 datasheet ESTIMATE (125 TFLOPS, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — NOT a same-machine A/B). The bare measured number is reported as-is; this single-16x16-coopmat-tile-per-workgroup kernel is EXPECTED to be a modest fraction of the cuBLAS estimate (it lacks register blocking / multi-warp tiles / double buffering) and the word 'competitive' is NOT used unless the measured % warrants it. The thesis-relevant deliverable is a real multi-tile coopmat matmul, BIT-EXACT, at X TFLOPS reported honestly — from one annotated .axc source → portable coopmat SPIR-V.

**PART C — working tiled attention (C1, NOT FA2).** tiled_attention.axc accumulators are scalar (already work); the zeros were dispatch-geometry/index bugs. Fixed to dispatch (seq_len,1,1) workgroups (one per query row); exp switched to a real exp2-based exp (OpExtInst GLSL.std.450 Exp2, exp(x)=exp2(x*log2e)); the CPU reference uses the IDENTICAL exp. NON-streaming full softmax (streaming FA2 online-softmax = C2, still M3.2b). AT-1630 upgraded to within-1e-3 bit-exact vs the CPU reference on Lavapipe+NVIDIA.

**Honesty.** The OpPhi gap was the coopmat-matmul root cause; the f32-matmul and attention zeros were separate scalar-path kernel-logic bugs (not OpPhi) and were debugged on the already-working Function-storage path. The matmul effective-TFLOPS is reported as the BARE measured number + % of the labeled 125-TFLOPS cuBLAS datasheet estimate, never asserted against a ratio and never described as 'competitive' unless the measured % warrants it — the honest deliverable is a real multi-tile coopmat matmul that is BIT-EXACT from one annotated source.
